title: Deploy event points at the wrong change
source: Live calls to Token Factory (Nemotron-3.5 Lightning)

evidence.claim: Concurrency rose from 1.0 (baseline) to 14.8 (incident) and varies within the incident window, explaining 0.506s of the 0.669s mean latency rise (slope 0.0367s per extra simultaneous request).
At high input tokens (1500-4000), low concurrency (0-2) yields median latency 0.48s, while high concurrency (10-inf) yields 1.07s, showing concurrency adds ~0.59s latency.
Retries are zero in both periods (baseline 0, incident 0), ruling out retry storm.

Prompt size increased from 213 to 3701 tokens but does not vary within the incident window (varies_in_incident_window=false); its effect is part of the unexplained 0.163s rise. At low concurrency, high prompt size only adds ~0.09s over baseline.

rejected_hypotheses.why_rejected: Stratified data shows high input tokens at low concurrency only increase median latency from 0.39s to 0.48s (+0.09s). Effect split attributes only unexplained 0.163s to prompt size (varies_in_incident_window=false), while concurrency explains 0.506s.
Retries are zero in both baseline and incident windows (pack_retries_baseline and pack_retries_incident show retries=0, share=1.0).
The latency rise is largely explained by client-side concurrency variation within the incident window (0.506s of 0.669s). No evidence of provider errors or latency spikes independent of concurrency.
The pack provides stratified comparisons, an effect-split model, and event context, allowing a clear determination that client concurrency is the dominant factor.

uncertainties: The prompt expansion effect is not fully separable from concurrency in the model; its exact contribution is uncertain but appears small.
Provider-side contention under high client concurrency cannot be ruled out entirely, but the linear concurrency-latency relationship suggests client-side queueing or rate limiting.
recommended_actions: Limit client-side concurrency (e.g., implement a semaphore or request queue) to keep simultaneous requests low.
Monitor concurrency metrics and set alerts for sudden increases.
Evaluate whether the top_k increase (retrieval from 2 to 40) is necessary; if not, revert to reduce prompt size and baseline latency.
Consider upgrading to a higher-throughput provider plan if concurrency is expected to remain high.

result.method: latency ~ the factors that vary inside the incident window, fitted on the incident window only
result.note: A factor with varies_in_incident_window=false changed between the normal period and the incident but cannot be told apart from the other changes in this window; its effect is in 'unexplained_s' if it matters.
